children: Apollo Global Management provided $1.25 billion in equity to help music company BMG repay outstanding liabilities to support its combination with independent label Concord.

Under the deal, the asset manager acquired a noncontrolling interest in a subsidiary of BMG, which holds Concord asset-backed securities backed by its catalog of more than 1 million songs. The equity investment allows BMG to repay certain of those outstanding asset-backed securities liabilities in an effort to boost the combined company's financial position, Apollo said Thursday.

"This transaction is indicative of Apollo's growing role as a provider of high-grade capital solutions to leading corporations across an expanding range of industries and use cases," Apollo Partner Jamshid Ehsani said.

BMG, the music arm of German media conglomerate Bertelsmann, combined with U.S.-based Concord in a cash-and-stock deal that closed on Sept. 1. Bertelsmann holds a 67% stake in the combined company, while Concord shareholders retained a 33% stake, managed by asset manager Great Mountain Partners.
The combined company, which retains the BMG name, aims to position itself to benefit from the age of artificial intelligence, with further investment in talent, technology and music rights.
